label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Recognizable restaurant reconstruction includes booth rows, pedestal tables and chairs, pendant lights, ceiling seams, tiled floor, corner windows and plants. Furniture and vegetation are simplified.
Left booths, central aisle, center/right dining furniture and rear/right window walls retain the main spatial arrangement. Spacing is more regular and open than the target.
Tables, seats and room height have plausible relative proportions. Chair backs and floor tiles are oversized relative to target details, without destroying functional recognition.

Light ceiling and tables contrast with darker seating, floor and pendant shades. Rectangular furniture and suspended dark fixtures preserve the main style, despite simplified silhouettes and uniform surface response.
Bright window regions and visible interior furniture broadly match the daylight setting. Heavy grain and flat illumination reduce quality, but major content remains identifiable.
Complementary views reveal furniture sides, pedestal supports and changing occlusion across a volumetric room, establishing genuine three-dimensional construction.

Actual hierarchy links locate architecture, booths, chairs and lamps with valid mesh children. Box.139 and Box.143 have nonempty mesh geometry and assigned tabletop/seating materials; Rod.010 supplies pedestal geometry and Ball supplies lamp volume. Materials contain connected surface shaders.

dimension_scores.evidence: Main restaurant identity is retained, but the elevated composition, sparse vegetation, blank windows and blocky furniture lose much of the target's specificity.
Individual chairs and tables show pedestal supports and lamps have suspension cords. Booth benches have inadequately explained support, and some furniture connections appear detached.
Grayscale tonal organization corresponds well; boxy seats, square bases and flattened lamp bodies approximate rather than reproduce the characteristic silhouettes.
Consistent perspective supports a believable room, but heavy render noise, primitive furniture, sticklike foliage and blank window panels produce a rough blockout appearance.
Booths and dining tables occupy corresponding sides around an aisle and adjacent window walls. Repetitive alignment, broader gaps and reduced planting simplify the spatial character.
Furniture heights and table-to-seat relationships are generally usable. Tall planar backs, large floor modules and short pendant drops weaken proportional similarity.
Scene remains legible with bright perimeter windows, but illumination is flat and noisy; glazing, upholstery and metal supports have weak visual differentiation.
Major architectural and furniture categories are present in substantial numbers. Dense planting, exterior window detail and finer furniture construction are substantially simplified.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
